title: How to create a new folder in Finder on Mac: steps for macOS 27
metaTitle: How to create a new folder in Finder on Mac: step by step
description: How to create a new folder in Finder on Mac: File > New Folder or Shift-Command-N, then type a name. Fixes for a greyed-out New Folder.

intro: To create a new folder in Finder on Mac, open a Finder window, then choose File > New Folder or press Shift-Command-N. Type a name and press Return, and the folder appears in the location that window shows.
tldr: Open a Finder window, then choose File > New Folder or press Shift-Command-N.
Type a name and press Return to finish. The folder lands where the active window points.
To nest a folder, open the parent folder first, then create the new one inside it.
If New Folder is greyed out, that location does not accept new folders. Check the drive, permissions and Locked box.

blocks.text: Finder is the file browser built into every Mac. Folders in Finder work like folders anywhere else. They hold files and other folders, and they keep a project tidy. Making one takes a few seconds once you know where the command lives. This guide covers the main method, the keyboard shortcut, nested folders, grouping existing files, iCloud Drive on the web, and what to do when New Folder is greyed out.
Create a folder from the File menu

Start with a Finder window. Click the Finder icon in the Dock, or press Command-N to open a new one. Next, open the place where the folder should live, such as Documents or Desktop. Then choose File > New Folder from the menu bar at the top of the screen. A folder appears with its name ready to edit. Type a name and press Return.

The menu command always acts on the active window. If you click a file inside another window, that window becomes the active one. So check the location before you choose the command. The path bar shows where you are at the bottom of the window. If you cannot see it, read [how to show the path bar in Finder](/how-to/show-the-path-bar-in-finder).

Apple's guide to organizing files says the same thing. Open a Finder window from the Dock and go to the location, or click the desktop. Then choose File > New Folder or press Shift-Command-N. Type a name, then press Return. The steps are the same on every current Mac that runs macOS 27.
Use the keyboard shortcut instead

Shift-Command-N creates a new folder in the active Finder window. Hold Shift and Command together, press N, and the folder appears. It is the fastest method once your fingers know it. Apple lists this shortcut on its Mac keyboard shortcuts page.

Watch out for two similar shortcuts. Command-N opens a new Finder window, not a folder. Option-Command-N makes a Smart Folder, which is not a regular folder. If you wanted an ordinary folder, use Shift-Command-N. The difference is small on screen, so read the name in the title bar before you type.

blocks.title: Smart Folder mix-up
blocks.text: If the new item does not behave like a plain folder, check whether you made a Smart Folder by accident. It has its own shortcut, Option-Command-N. A regular folder uses Shift-Command-N.
Make a folder inside another folder

To nest a folder, open the folder that should hold it first. Double-click the parent folder so its window is active. Then create the new folder while that window is in front. Finder places the new folder inside the one you have open. Nested folders keep long projects readable, so this is worth a habit.

A common mistake is creating a folder in the wrong window. You open Documents, then create the folder while the Desktop window is still active. The new folder lands on the Desktop. Look at the path bar, then drag the folder into the right place if it ended up somewhere odd. Dragging is a normal Finder move, so nothing else changes.

items: Double-click the parent folder to open it.
Confirm the path bar shows the parent folder name.
Choose File > New Folder or press Shift-Command-N.
Type the name and press Return.

blocks.text: Group existing files into a new folder

You can also create a folder around files you have already picked. Select the items first. Control-click one of the selected items. Choose New Folder with Selection from the menu that opens. Name the folder, then press Return. Finder groups the selected items inside the new folder.

This is faster than creating an empty folder and dragging items in one at a time. It works well for a stack of screenshots or a set of invoices. Check the result afterward. Grouping changes where the files live, so a quick look confirms you got the right set.
Create a folder on the Desktop

The Desktop counts as a location. Click an empty part of the Desktop so Finder treats it as the active place. Then choose File > New Folder. The new folder appears on the Desktop. Desktop folders are handy for a short project, but they crowd the screen fast. Move them into Documents when the work is done.
Create a folder in iCloud Drive on the web

Finder is Mac only. If you are on another computer, or you want to add a folder from a browser, use iCloud.com. Go to icloud.com/iclouddrive and sign in with your Apple Account if you are asked to. Click the New Folder button in the iCloud Drive toolbar. The folder appears in the current view.

The web version has its own rules. To nest a folder, open the parent folder first. The New Folder button does not appear in Recents or Recently Deleted. To rename a folder, select it, click the More button in the top-right corner, choose Rename, and type the new name.
Why New Folder is greyed out

Apple's folder page says it plainly. If the New Folder command is dimmed, you cannot create a folder in the current location. The command is not broken. The location is refusing new items. The fix is usually in the drive, the permissions or the sync setup.

items: An NTFS drive. According to iBoysoft, macOS can't write to NTFS drives without extra software.
A read-only volume, such as a disk image or a read-only location.
Your account lacks Read & Write access to the folder.
The Locked box is checked in Get Info.
A write-protect switch on an SD card or USB stick is set.
A sync app, such as OneDrive, is temporarily blocking new folders.

rows: Folder you own, with Read & Write access
Use a drive formatted for macOS
Copy the files to a writable location
SD card with write-protect switch on
Slide the switch, then reinsert the card
blocks.caption: Where New Folder usually works and where it does not.

blocks.text: Start with the drive. Open Disk Utility to see how the volume is formatted. If it is an NTFS drive, you need a different drive or a macOS-friendly format. Reformatting erases the drive, so back it up first. Do not skip that step.

For folder permissions, select the folder and open Get Info. Uncheck Locked if it is checked. If the padlock is closed, click it and sign in, then set Read & Write for your account under Sharing & Permissions. iBoysoft describes the same steps for APFS and Mac OS Extended volumes.

Run First Aid in Disk Utility if the drive seems damaged. iBoysoft also suggests creating the folder in Terminal with cd and mkdir. That works, but it is a poor first choice for most people. Try the Finder fixes first, and relaunch Finder if the window stays stuck.

blocks.title: Leave System Integrity Protection alone
blocks.text: Some guides say to turn off System Integrity Protection from Recovery Mode when a system volume is read-only. That weakens system security. Do not do it just to make one folder. Pick a writable location instead.
Common mistakes people make

items: Creating the folder in the wrong window. Check the path bar before you press Shift-Command-N.
Making a Smart Folder by mistake. Use Shift-Command-N for a plain folder.
Trying to nest from Recents on iCloud.com. Open the parent folder first.
Ignoring the Locked box. A folder can look normal and still refuse new items.
Forgetting to press Return. Finish the name with Return so the change sticks.

blocks.text: A new folder only helps if you can find it again. Tags are a good next step when a folder crosses several projects. Read [how to add a tag to a file in Finder](/how-to/add-a-tag-to-a-file-in-finder) for that. If you need the same folder from another spot, [create an alias in Finder](/how-to/create-an-alias-in-finder) instead of copying it.
Where Lazur helps with this

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold Option and Command, then ask your question out loud. Lazur looks at your screen, points at the control, and answers out loud. For this task, ask where New Folder is. Lazur circles the command and labels it.

Lazur does not click for you. If you ask how to do something, it guides you one click at a time and waits for each click. The clicks are still yours. Its privacy notes say it listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Lazur runs on the Mac only, and Windows is planned, not available. You can read more on [the Finder page](/apps/finder).
Quick checks before you finish

items: The path bar shows the location you meant.
The folder sits in the window where you expect it.
New Folder is not dimmed in that window.
The name is spelled the way you want it.

blocks.text: If something is off, check the window first, then the drive, then the permissions. That order fixes most cases. If you get stuck in a menu, hold Option and Command and ask Lazur where the command is.

faq.question: Can I make a folder without a Finder window?
faq.answer: Not really. Finder needs a location, and the Desktop counts as one. Click an empty part of the Desktop, then choose File > New Folder. The folder appears on the Desktop.

faq.question: What is the shortcut for a new folder in Finder?
faq.answer: Press Shift-Command-N with a Finder window active. Apple lists this shortcut on its Mac keyboard shortcuts page. Do not confuse it with Option-Command-N, which makes a Smart Folder.

faq.question: Why is New Folder greyed out on my Mac?
faq.answer: A dimmed New Folder means the current location will not take a new folder. Common causes are an NTFS drive, a read-only disk image, missing Read & Write access, the Locked box, a write-protect switch or a sync app.

faq.question: How do I make a folder inside another folder on Mac?
faq.answer: Double-click the parent folder to open it. Then choose File > New Folder while that window is active. The new folder goes inside the one you have open.

faq.question: Can I create a folder in iCloud Drive from any computer?
faq.answer: Yes, through a browser. Go to icloud.com/iclouddrive, sign in, and click New Folder in the iCloud Drive toolbar. Finder itself is Mac only, so the web version is the route for other computers.

faq.question: Is a Smart Folder the same as a regular folder?
faq.answer: No. Option-Command-N creates a Smart Folder, which Apple lists separately from regular folders. Use Shift-Command-N when you want an ordinary folder.

faq.question: Does Lazur create the folder for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at the New Folder command and can guide you one click at a time, waiting for each click. You do the clicking, because Lazur does not operate other apps for you.

steps.name: Open a Finder window
steps.text: Click the Finder icon in the Dock, or choose File > New Finder Window. Command-N does the same job from the keyboard.
steps.tip: Use one window per location so the path bar is easy to read.

steps.name: Open the target location
steps.text: Double-click Documents, Desktop, or any folder in the sidebar. The window should show the place where the new folder belongs. Check the path bar at the bottom of the window before you go on.
steps.tip: If you cannot see the path bar, show it first. Its guide explains how.

steps.name: Choose New Folder
steps.text: With the window active, open the File menu and choose New Folder. If the command is dimmed, stop here and read the greyed-out section of this guide.
steps.tip: The shortcut works the same way, so skip the menu once you know it.

steps.name: Type the name
steps.text: A new folder appears with its name ready to edit. Type the name you want. Keep it short and specific, such as Invoices or Tax receipts.

steps.name: Press Return
steps.text: Press Return to confirm the name. The folder now sits in that location, ready to hold files.

steps.name: Check where it landed
steps.text: Look at the folder in the window and at the path bar. If it landed in the wrong place, drag it to the right folder. Dragging is a normal Finder move.
steps.tip: Read the path bar again after any move, so you know where the folder ended up.

troubleshooting.problem: New Folder is greyed out in a window
troubleshooting.fix: Apple says a dimmed New Folder command means you cannot create a folder in that location. Click a different window or location and try again. If it stays dimmed, check the drive, permissions and Locked box in the sections above.

troubleshooting.problem: New Folder is greyed out on an external drive
troubleshooting.fix: macOS can't write to NTFS drives without extra software, according to iBoysoft. Use a drive formatted for macOS, such as APFS or Mac OS Extended. Back up the drive first, because reformatting erases it.

troubleshooting.problem: Folder is Locked and won't accept new items
troubleshooting.fix: Select the folder and open Get Info. Uncheck Locked, click the padlock if it is closed and sign in, then set Read & Write for your account under Sharing & Permissions.

troubleshooting.problem: SD card or USB stick refuses new folders
troubleshooting.fix: Check for a physical write-protect switch on the card or drive. Slide it to the unlocked position, reinsert the media, and try again.

troubleshooting.problem: A sync app stops new folders from appearing
troubleshooting.fix: Sync apps such as OneDrive can block folder creation for a short time. Pause sync, wait a moment, then try again. Resume sync when you are done.

troubleshooting.problem: Finder feels stuck and the command does nothing
troubleshooting.fix: Relaunch Finder, then open a fresh window and try File > New Folder again. Run First Aid in Disk Utility if the drive still acts up.
